memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: or casts spells, or who is a medium or spiritist or who consults the dead. Anyone who does these things is detestable to the Lord; because of these same detestable practices the Lord your God will drive out those nations before you. You must be blameless before the Lord your God. - Deut 18:11-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God continues His list, casting spells, consulting mediums and spiritists, seeking the dead. Then He states clearly why these are so serious, "Anyone who does these things is detestable to the Lord." In fact, it was for exactly these practices that God was driving out the nations from the land. The call to His people is plain, "You must be blameless before the Lord your God."

Seeking the dead or turning to mediums is not a neutral curiosity. It is a turning away from the living God to hidden and deceptive spiritual sources. God calls this detestable not because He is harsh, but because such practices deceive people and lead them away from Him, the only true source of comfort and guidance.

We may face grief so deep that we long to reach across to loved ones who have died. But God, in His kindness, forbids these paths because they cannot help us and only draw us into danger and deception. Instead, He offers Himself. In Christ, we have a living hope beyond the grave and a comfort no medium could ever give (1 Thess 4:13-14). The call to be "blameless" points us to the One who was truly blameless, Jesus, in whom we are made clean. When you are anxious or grieving, where do you turn for comfort and answers?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do you turn when you are anxious or grieving?
2. How does the hope of resurrection in Christ comfort you?
3. What would it mean to seek God alone for your answers?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, when I grieve or long for answers, keep me turning to You. Thank You for the living hope I have in Jesus. Amen.
